benchmarking_db 1352. Brandon's decision: ADR-0001's strict reading is the project-wide ERR33-C labeling bar -- a call ERR33-C covers whose result is not tested is a violation as written, and EX1 does not exempt it. valkey was already labeled to that bar (bmdb 1340, source aafab15); the other projects were not, so a per-rule ERR33-C figure mixed two bars. This batch corrects the non-valkey side.

THE BAR, READ OFF valkey RATHER THAN PARAPHRASED. All 47 valkey ERR33-C FPs say one thing: the flagged call's own return value IS tested before use -- NULL sentinel, endptr, range check, truncation predicate, loop controlling expression, an unconditional assert. None is justified by "cannot fail", "unactionable", "provably cannot truncate", "idiomatic" or "the value is used later". So FP means the error indicator is tested, and everything else is TP.

SELECTION, two independent passes that had to agree. (1) A read of every non-valkey ERR33-C FP reason, classified into "the analyzer misread" vs "the value is untested and that is justified on context". (2) A syntactic screen of the source at each project's pinned commit: what form the call takes (bare statement, (void) cast, assignment, inside a condition) and, for an assignment, whether the target ever reaches a controlling expression later in the same function. 185 rows where both passes say flip are corrected here. Where they disagreed, the row was read at the pinned commit and either resolved or parked; no row was flipped on the reason text alone. That mattered: raylib's "unchecked stdlib return advisory" template does not describe the code (src/rtext.c:2605 really does test readVars < 4 three lines down, and stays FP).

CONTENT. 185 rows across 7 projects -- raylib 54, curl 47, mosquitto 40, sqlite 29, hostap 9, lua 5, libcrc 1. By form: 121 bare call statements (the result discarded outright) and 64 assignments whose target is never tested anywhere in the enclosing function. By callee family: formatted-output 85, stream-io 56, time 23, formatted-input 9, process 7, conversion-locale 3, environment 2. By callee: snprintf 54, sprintf 29, fflush 26, time 23, fseek 15, fwrite 13, sscanf 9, atexit 3, signal 3, setlocale 2, ungetc 2, vsnprintf 2, getenv 2, raise 1, strftime 1. pureftpd (0 of 170 FPs) and mbedtls (0 of 17) move by nothing: their ERR33-C FPs are genuine assign-in-condition NULL tests the rule misses, so those two projects were already comparable with valkey. Three sub-shapes carry most of the delta -- bare fflush/fwrite/fseek on debug and cleanup paths, "the buffer is exactly sized so snprintf cannot truncate", and time(NULL) as a timer or expiry baseline. valkey labeled all three TP.

FOR BRANDON TO VETO SEPARATELY: the 29 raylib sprintf rows (src/rmodels.c, src/raudio.c, src/rtext.c -- the 'byteCount += sprintf(...)' export accumulators). They flip on the general rule, not on a matched precedent: valkey has no sprintf findings at all, so the nearest precedent is its 'config.last_printed_bytes += printf(...)' TP. Removing them is a clean subset -- they are the only sprintf rows in the batch.

LIVENESS NOT RE-VERIFIED, unlike task-1281, which confirmed its 57 keys still fired at run 261. These 185 are existing keys in this repo's CSVs, corrected where they sit; no new scan was run for this batch. A label is a statement about the code at the pinned commit rather than about a run, so the correction stands either way, but the distinction is recorded rather than glossed.

MECHANICS, following task-1281. Each corrected row carries this batch's source and a reason quoting the one it supersedes; the 17 source manifests get row_count decrements and superseded_rows records. The CSVs went through a csv round trip verified byte-stable against all 12 files beforehand, so the diff is exactly 185 additions and 185 deletions -- add equals delete in every file, key sets identical and in the same order, 0 duplicates, no row lost or gained. Reasons are label basis only.

Adjudicator claude-opus-5 on dev-180. Counting basis: distinct (project, commit, file, line, rule) keys. No precision/recall claim is made here; an ERR33-C figure computed before this lands mixes two bars, one computed after does not.
